I have 20 mu, and for my land the safe way is still wheat followed by maize. I only finished primary school, so I do not calculate too fancy. I mostly look at what worked on my own fields and what the better farmers in the village do. Last few years, if wheat gets too little fertilizer, the heads are small, and if maize misses the early growth, it never really catches up. But money is also tight, because some people in my family work outside and cash must be kept for daily life. So this year I will stay with the usual wheat-maize rotation on all 20 mu, use improved seed that people nearby commonly buy, put most money into fertilizer and the key irrigations, and not spend too much on extra chemicals unless I really see a problem.

For wheat, I will sow in early October after getting the field ready with rotary tillage, put base fertilizer first, then topdress once at jointing if the stand looks all right. Wheat needs water more steadily here, so I plan a few well irrigations, but not too many because pumping costs money. After wheat harvest in June, I will move fast into summer maize. The gap is short, so I will do simple tillage or direct seeding after a quick field clean-up, use hybrid maize seed, give enough fertilizer early, and watch the rain. If summer rain is decent, I may only irrigate once or twice. For pesticides, I do what most neighbors do: herbicide first, then insecticide only if I see real pressure.
